summary: What a wife finds and what she earns belong to her husband, and he eats the fruits of what she inherits. Payments for her shame and damage are hers, and Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira says the husband gets a share.

chunks.en: What a wife finds and what she earns with her hands
chunks.st: object found by a wife and the wife’s earnings belong

chunks.en: belong to her husband. And her inheritance,
chunks.st: to her husband. And with regard to her inheritance,

chunks.en: he eats its fruits while she is alive.
chunks.st: the husband enjoys the profits of this property in her lifetime.
chunks.stMore: If she is humiliated or injured, the perpetrator is liable to pay compensation for

chunks.en: The payment for her shame and her damage
chunks.explain: If someone embarrassed or hurt her.
chunks.st: her humiliation and her degradation, as relevant.

chunks.he: שֶׁלָּהּ. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶן בְּתֵירָא אוֹמֵר,
chunks.en: is hers. Rabbi Yehudah ben Beseira says,
chunks.st: This payment belongs to her. Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:

chunks.en: when the hurt is in a hidden place,
chunks.st: When it is an injury that is in a concealed part of the woman’s body,

words.en: that it is in the hidden place

chunks.en: she gets two parts,
chunks.st: she receives two parts,
chunks.stMore: i.e., two-thirds, of the payment for humiliation and degradation,

chunks.en: and he gets one.
chunks.st: and the husband receives one
chunks.stMore: part, i.e., one-third, as the injury affects him as well.

chunks.en: And when the hurt is in a place that shows,
chunks.st: And when it is an injury that is in an exposed part of her body,

words.en: that it is in the open place

chunks.en: he gets two parts,
chunks.st: he receives two parts,
chunks.stMore: as he suffers public humiliation due to her condition,

chunks.en: and she gets one.
chunks.st: and she receives one part.

chunks.en: His share is given right away.
chunks.st: His payment should be given to him immediately.

chunks.en: And with hers, land is bought,
chunks.st: And with her portion, land should be purchased with it,

chunks.en: and he eats its fruits.
chunks.st: and he enjoys the profits of that property.

summary: A man promised money to his son-in-law, and the son-in-law died. The Sages say he may tell the brother who marries the widow, I wanted to give it to your brother, not to you.

chunks.en: One who promised money to his son-in-law,
chunks.st: one who pledges to set aside a sum of money for his son-in-law as part of a dowry,

chunks.en: and his son-in-law died,
chunks.st: and his son-in-law dies
chunks.stMore: before receiving the money, the terms of the dowry do not transfer to the brother, who is now the yavam of the widow.

chunks.en: the Sages said,
chunks.st: The Sages said:

chunks.en: he can say,
chunks.st: The father-in-law can say to the yavam:

chunks.en: To your brother I wanted to give,
chunks.st: To your brother, I wanted to give this money,

chunks.en: but to you I do not want to give.
chunks.st: but to you I do not want to give it.

summary: When a kallah brings money or goods into the marriage, the chasan writes a bigger amount in the kesubah for money and a smaller amount for goods. Goods were usually valued at more than they were really worth.
stIntro: The mishna addresses another matter. If the woman had

chunks.en: If she promised to bring him a thousand dinar,
chunks.st: pledged to bring in for him one thousand dinars in cash as a dowry,

chunks.he: הוּא פוֹסֵק כְּנֶגְדָּן חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר מָנֶה.
chunks.en: he promises fifteen hundred against them.
chunks.explain: He can earn money using cash.
chunks.st: he then pledges, in the marriage contract, that he will give her fifteen hundred dinars against them.
chunks.stMore: That is, he writes in the marriage document that in the event of divorce or his death, he will pay her that greater amount.

chunks.en: And against goods that were valued,
chunks.st: And against the appraisal
chunks.stMore: of goods such as utensils and other movable items that are included in the dowry,

chunks.en: he promises one fifth less.
chunks.st: he pledges one-fifth less
chunks.stMore: than the amount of the evaluation. This is because movable property is generally assessed at a value one-fifth higher than the actual value, and he cannot earn any money from these items.

chunks.en: If they were valued at one hundred and are really worth one hundred,
chunks.st: If the appraisal is set at one hundred dinars and the property is actually worth one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: he has only one hundred.
chunks.st: then since the appraisal is conducted at market value he has a claim to property worth only one hundred dinars.
chunks.stMore: Likewise, he may not record a decreased sum of property. His recorded

chunks.en: For a valuation of one hundred,
chunks.st: appraisal of the movable property that she brings into the marriage is one hundred dinars only when

chunks.he: הִיא נוֹתֶנֶת שְׁלֹשִׁים וְאֶחָד סֶלַע וְדִינָר.
chunks.en: she must give thirty-one sela and a dinar.
chunks.st: she is giving thirty-one sela and one dinar,
chunks.stMore: equal to 125 dinars. This is because the actual value is one-fifth less than the inflated evaluation, as explained.

chunks.en: And for four hundred,
chunks.st: And similarly, he pledges four hundred dinars against her assets only when

chunks.en: she gives five hundred.
chunks.st: she is giving five hundred,
chunks.stMore: based on the inflated assessment of their worth, such that the real value is four hundred dinars.

chunks.en: What the chasan promises,
chunks.st: In contrast, what the son-in-law pledges
chunks.stMore: according to the amount of the dowry that the bride brings,

chunks.en: he promises one fifth less.
chunks.st: he pledges one-fifth less
chunks.stMore: in the marriage contract, which is the actual value of the property.

summary: If the kallah brings money, each sela counts as more in the kesubah. The chasan also gives money for her needs, and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says it all follows the custom of the place.

chunks.en: If she promised to bring him money,
chunks.st: she pledged to bring him money and not articles to serve as a dowry,

chunks.en: a silver sela becomes six dinars.
chunks.st: her sela, i.e., four dinars, becomes six
chunks.stMore: dinars with respect to the husband’s obligation in the marriage contract. This follows the standard outlined in the previous mishna: The groom increases his obligation by one half since he will profit from this money.

chunks.he: הֶחָתָן מְקַבֵּל עָלָיו עֲשָׂרָה דִינָרִין לַקֻּפָּה,
chunks.en: The chasan takes on himself ten dinars for her purse
chunks.st: Additionally, the groom accepts upon himself to give ten dinars to the account for her needs,

chunks.en: for every hundred.
chunks.st: for each and every hundred dinars that she brings.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.en: It all follows the custom of the land.
chunks.st: Everything is in accordance with the regional custom.

summary: A father who marries off his daughter must give her at least fifty zuz. A chasan must dress his kallah before she leaves her father's house, and the tzedakah fund helps an orphan girl get married.

chunks.en: One who marries off his daughter without saying how much,
chunks.st: one who marries off his daughter with the terms of the dowry unspecified,

chunks.en: must not give her less than fifty zuz.
chunks.st: he must not give her less than fifty dinars.

chunks.en: If he promised to bring her in with nothing,
chunks.st: If the bride’s father pledged to bring her into the marriage bare,
chunks.stMore: by saying that he refuses to give her anything,

chunks.en: the husband should not say, When I bring her
chunks.st: the husband should not say: When I bring her

chunks.en: into my house I will dress her in my clothes.
chunks.st: into my house, I will clothe her with my clothing, but not beforehand.

chunks.en: Rather, he dresses her while she is still in her father's house.
chunks.st: Rather, he must clothe her while she is yet in her father’s house,
chunks.stMore: and she enters the marriage with the clothing in hand.

chunks.en: And also one who marries off an orphan girl
chunks.st: And similarly, with regard to a charity administrator who marries off an orphan girl, he

chunks.en: must not give her less than fifty zuz.
chunks.st: must not give her less than fifty dinars.

chunks.en: If there is money in the tzedakah box,
chunks.st: If there are sufficient resources in the charity fund,

chunks.en: we provide for her as fits her honor.
chunks.st: the charities provide even more for her, furnishing a dowry and her other needs according to her dignity.

summary: An orphan girl who was married off with a small dowry can later get her proper share from the family's property. Rabbi Yehudah and the Sages argue about how to know how much she should get.

chunks.he: יְתוֹמָה שֶׁהִשִּׂיאַתָּה אִמָּהּ אוֹ אַחֶיהָ מִדַּעְתָּהּ,
chunks.en: An orphan girl whose mother or brothers married her off with her agreement,
chunks.st: orphan girl whose mother or brothers married her off, even with her consent
chunks.stMore: to a small dowry, she retains her rights to a proper dowry.

chunks.he: וְכָתְבוּ לָהּ בְּמֵאָה אוֹ בַחֲמִשִּׁים זוּז,
chunks.en: and they wrote for her one hundred or fifty zuz,
chunks.st: And thus, if they wrote for her a dowry of one hundred or of fifty dinars,

chunks.en: when she grows up, she can take from them
chunks.st: she may, upon reaching majority, exact from
chunks.stMore: her mother, or brothers, or their respective estates the sum of money

chunks.en: what she should really get.
chunks.st: that is fit to be given to her
chunks.stMore: as a dowry, which is one-tenth of the family’s estate. Even if she agreed to forgo part of this sum as a minor, she may collect it as an adult.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: If the father married off the first daughter,
chunks.st: If the father married off the first daughter before he died,

chunks.en: the second gets the same as he gave the first.
chunks.st: a dowry should be given to the second daughter in the same manner that he gave one to the first daughter.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say: There is no ready standard, since

chunks.en: sometimes a person is poor and becomes rich,
chunks.st: sometimes a person is poor and then becomes wealthy,

chunks.en: or rich and becomes poor.
chunks.st: or a person is wealthy and then becomes poor,
chunks.stMore: so a family’s allowance for dowries is subject to change.

chunks.he: אֶלָּא שָׁמִין אֶת הַנְּכָסִים וְנוֹתְנִין לָהּ:
chunks.en: Rather, we value the property and give her.
chunks.explain: She gets a tenth of the property.
chunks.st: Rather, the court appraises the property and gives her the appropriate sum.

summary: A father left money with a third person to buy a field for his daughter. Rabbi Meir says the third person must do as he was told; Rabbi Yosei says a grown daughter may decide.

chunks.en: One who gives money to a third person for his daughter,
chunks.st: one who transfers money by means of a third party for his daughter
chunks.stMore: to purchase a field after she marries, is the daughter allowed to assert control over the money?

words.en: the one who gives to a third person

chunks.en: and she says, I trust my husband,
chunks.st: If she says after she marries: My husband is trustworthy for me,
chunks.stMore: so give him the money to buy the property for me, her wishes are not honored.

chunks.en: the third person must do what he was trusted with.
chunks.st: The third party should execute the agency that was entrusted in his power;

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Meir says.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: If it were only a field
chunks.st: The daughter has authority: And were it only a field

chunks.en: and she wanted to sell it,
chunks.st: and she wanted to sell it,

chunks.en: it would be sold right away!
chunks.st: it could be sold immediately.
chunks.stMore: Just as she would have authority to control the field, she may control the money assigned for her.

chunks.en: When is this said?
chunks.st: The mishna qualifies: In what case is this statement said?

chunks.en: About a grown woman. But a young girl,
chunks.st: With respect to an adult woman. But with respect to a minor girl,

chunks.en: what a young girl does means nothing.
chunks.st: any action of a minor girl is nothing
chunks.stMore: from a legal standpoint; a minor would have no authority in this matter.
